commands.review_summary:
The branch adds collection-aware stale app-state recovery, durable generation-based replay intents, ordered event persistence, SQLite migrations, and extensive regression coverage for chat-state writes.

Reproducibility: yes. The PR documents authenticated stale-key and corrupted-LTHash reproductions that caused chat writes to fail or risk stale local state, and the affected source path is covered by focused regressions.

target.title: fix(telegram): duplicate inbound messages after a transient update-offset persistence failure
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Telegram users on a self-hosted OpenClaw gateway can have
already-handled inbound messages re-delivered and re-processed after a restart,
producing duplicate replies and duplicate side effects (re-run tools/commands).

The trigger is a *transient* failure while persisting the Telegram Bot API
update offset (the durable watermark the gateway saves so it can resume without
replaying old updates). Any temporary hiccup in the plugin state store (disk I/O
error, lock contention, quota) makes the offset write fail. When that happens
the gateway logs the error but never catches the offset back up, so the durable
offset silently drifts behind the position the gateway has actually processed.
On the next restart the bot resumes from that stale offset and Telegram
re-delivers everything after it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The update tracker coalesces offset writes behind a single in-flight write and a
monotonic "highest requested" high-water mark. Previously, when a write threw,
`drainPersistQueue` only reported the error: it dropped the pending target and
left the request high-water mark advanced, so (1) the failed offset was never
retried and (2) a later request for the same offset was short-circuited by the
`updateId <= highestPersistenceRequestedUpdateId` guard. The durable offset
could then only ever move again if some strictly higher offset happened to
persist successfully.

This change makes offset persistence resilient to transient failures without
touching the coalescing fast path or any public API:

- On a failed write it keeps the durable watermark unchanged (unchanged
  behavior), re-arms the failed offset (unless a newer coalesced target already
  supersedes it), and rolls the request high-water mark back to the durable
  floor so the same offset can be requested and retried.
- It retries on a bounded exponential backoff (250ms up to 5s, `unref`ed) so a
  temporary storage outage recovers even on an idle chat, while a persistently
  failing writer cannot hot-spin the event loop.
- On success it resets the backoff.

The safe-completed watermark still fences the offset behind any pending or
failed update, so a retry never advances the offset past an update that is still
in flight.

### Follow-up: tie the retry to the bot lifecycle (addresses ClawSweeper review)

The first revision left the retry timer detached from the owning bot. Telegram
account removal and token changes deliberately delete the persisted offset, and
`bot.stop()` did not dispose the tracker — so a queued retry from a retired
tracker could wake after shutdown and write an already-retired offset back into
the shared account store, creating a *second* stale-offset path.

This revision gives the retry explicit lifecycle ownership:

- `createTelegramUpdateTracker` now exposes `dispose()`, which clears the pending
  retry timer and latches a `disposed` flag so no scheduled or in-flight write
  can persist afterwards.
- `bot-core.ts` invokes `updateTracker.dispose()` from the existing `bot.stop`
  hook (alongside the thread-binding and outbound-recorder teardown), aligning
  the tracker's lifetime with the bot.
- `drainPersistQueue` yields to disposal if it races an in-flight write, so it
  never re-arms a retry for an offset that is being retired on purpose.

## User Impact

Telegram channels no longer re-deliver and re-answer already-processed messages
after a gateway restart that followed a transient state-store error. Operators
get an offset that reliably catches up to the processed position once the
underlying storage recovers, instead of a watermark that stays stuck until new,
higher-numbered traffic arrives.

## Evidence

Added focused regression tests in
`extensions/telegram/src/bot-update-tracker.test.ts` and validated the full
tracker suite plus the closest offset/persistence integration tests.

- `vitest run extensions/telegram/src/bot-update-tracker.test.ts` -> **18 passed
  (18)** (13 existing + 5 new).
- Before/after proof: temporarily reverting the retry fix makes
  `retries a transient offset persistence failure until it succeeds` and
  `keeps retrying offset persistence across repeated transient failures` report
  `expected "vi.fn()" to be called 2 times, but got 1 times`; reverting the
  `dispose()` wiring makes `cancels a scheduled offset-persistence retry once
  disposed` fail with the retry firing after shutdown. With the fix, all 18 pass.
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on all changed files -> clean.

New tests:

1. `retries a transient offset persistence failure until it succeeds` -- one
   transient failure; the durable offset does not advance, the error is
   surfaced, and a timer-driven retry (no new traffic) persists the offset.
2. `keeps retrying offset persistence across repeated transient failures` --
   three consecutive failures back off and eventually succeed.
3. `does not persist a higher offset past an id whose write is still failing` --
   with a later update still pending, retries land the offset exactly on the
   safe id and never jump past the unfinished update.
4. `cancels a scheduled offset-persistence retry once disposed` -- after a failed
   write schedules a retry, `dispose()` clears the timer and no further write
   happens even after the backoff window elapses (stop/reconfiguration race).
5. `ignores new offset-persistence requests after being disposed` -- a disposed
   tracker does not resurrect persistence for freshly handled updates.
